relatedNodes.html: This is an ideal place to visit for nature lovers. The city’s botanical gardens consist of 4,500 flowers and a thousand species of wildlife. It also has a huge collection of orchids, a butterfly garden, and a cactus garden.

Plaza Botero, named after the hometown hero Fernando Botero, houses 23 humongous sculptures that have now become the city’s most iconic symbol. More of the artist’s works are displayed in Museo de Antioquia, which is arguably the most photographed place in the entire country.
Museo de Antioquia not only displays a bunch of Botero’s sculptures but it’s also a home to numerous pre-Colombian works of other famous artists (both national and international).
If you are a foodie, this is the best place to go for a date. Let your Colombian woman be your guide to the best Colombian dishes. You can even watch how Medellin’s local favorites are cooked.
Toucan café particularly offers street food. So if you want to try some more exotic dishes, don’t miss the kind of cuisine paisas take pride in.

This is a mock town on top of Cerro Nutibara, which is like a living museum. When you visit, it’s almost like you’re actually in ancient Antioquia. The village consists of a mayor's office, one-room schoolhouse, traditional town square, and a barbershop.
But there are also a lot of handicraft and souvenir shops you can check out as well. And if you are on a date, there are also noteworthy restaurants you can bring your date to.
You can even try the classical dishes in the village, such as a belly-busting platter of ground meat, avocados served with rice and refried beans, fried plantains, pork cracklings, and bandeja paisa.

What’s unique about this park is visitors are encouraged to take off their shoes when wandering through the sandy pits, green gardens, and bubbling water fountains. This way, you get to experience and feel different textures.

The purpose of this park is to reconnect with nature the way ancient humans originally did. This is the most beloved and bizarre part of the city which you and your date will surely enjoy, so take a romantic walk around this park.

This place is an interactive science museum with 300 interactive exhibits inside the building’s four red cubes. There’s also a television studio, planetarium, and 3D auditorium. Interestingly, it also houses South America’s largest freshwater aquarium.
Conveniently, it’s near the shopping malls and botanical gardens. So, after you and your date are done experiencing Parque Explora, there are places nearby where you can unwind.

This is probably the place in Medellin where most tourists stay because it has plenty of hotels, inns, and other forms of accommodation. But there are also plenty of high-end restaurants and cafės all around, so you and your date don’t have to go far for a place to unwind.
